short: Logical qubits and spacetime cost bound

lean.name: DynamicCircuit.count
lean.plain: Gate count with a maximum at each conditional
lean.annotation: In `DynamicCircuit.count` a measurement adds zero to a $T$ count. A conditional with branches of cost 3 and 7 contributes 7, and consecutive pieces contribute the sum of their counts. Taking each maximum separately bounds every execution, even when the most expensive branches cannot all occur together.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.stoppingPowerAncillas
lean.annotation: Appendix G.4 divides the 390 ancillas into 42 for total electron momentum, 48 for the phase-gradient state, 87 for block-encoding control and data, and 213 for workspace. The first two registers retain data used across walk steps. All 390 qubits start clean at the beginning of each evolution.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.StoppingPower.systemQubits
lean.annotation: The solution and the baseline both use the same $3(218\cdot6+8)=3{,}948$ system qubits. The ancilla counts are 1,702 and 390, respectively, for the baseline and the solution. The ratio of total widths is $5{,}650/4{,}338\approx1.30$.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.stoppingPower_const_cost
lean.annotation: Appendix G.4 reports about 59,600 initialization T gates per run. `stoppingPower_const_cost` gives an aggregate upper bound of 229,357,900,876,653,900 logical-qubit × T-count units for 50 runs at each of ten times, and separately rules out primitive `TOFF` gates at every time.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.stoppingPowerConstCost
lean.annotation: Dividing `stoppingPowerConstCost` by $50\cdot4{,}338$ gives $1{,}057{,}436{,}149{,}731$, the $T$-count cap for one execution at each of the ten times. Dividing by ten gives the reported average of about $1.06\times10^{11}$ $T$ gates per run.

statements.note: The fusion row reports mean logical spacetime cost per evolution across 500 runs, not a cost bound for every individual evolution time. Appendix G.4 reports 229,357,900,876,653,900 qubit–T in total, or about 4.59 × 10¹⁴ per run; Figure 3a compares that mean with the authors' baseline of 5.42 × 10¹⁵ per run.
